items.title: Apps and programming: two accidental tyrannies
items.summary: A talk transcript from MIT's HCI Seminar where Matuschak argues that app silos and programming's role as a specialised skill have together strangled interface invention — and shows, with live demos, how composable software architectures and coding agents can begin to undo both.
items.why: The core claim is that coding agents now let designers prototype complex, novel interactions without waiting on engineers — Matuschak shows this working in practice. Directly applicable to how CueDesign could move faster on experimental UX for Cuemath's learning flows.

items.title: A calmer interface for a product in motion
items.summary: How two Linear engineers — new to the codebase — shipped a full UI refresh using Claude Code and Cursor as execution partners, including building a custom colour-picker dev tool on the fly to iterate on design tokens without freezing feature work.
items.why: The concrete case study for using coding agents as design-execution partners: a two-person team, unfamiliar with the codebase, shipped a coherent system-wide refresh in months. A model worth studying for small design-system teams like CueDesign.

items.title: The Typography of whitehouse.gov, 2000–2026
items.summary: A deep typographic analysis tracing how six US presidential administrations chose website typefaces — from Bush's embedded system fonts to Obama's Hoefler commissions to Trump's pivot to free Google Fonts — reading each decision as a political and cultural allegory.
items.why: A masterclass in how font choice encodes institutional values at a glance — the same logic applies when Cuemath picks type that must signal both academic credibility to parents and warmth and play to kids simultaneously.

items.title: Pangram Pangram's Neue Gstaad is a mountainous homage to Swiss excellence
items.summary: Pangram Pangram's new release — 112 styles across seven subfamilies, designed by Ian Party — draws on Swiss mountain culture to build a typeface system built for extreme range, from compressed editorial to large-scale environmental use.
items.why: A strong reference for how a type system can be designed to flex across every scale without losing character — relevant to how a design system like CueDesign specifies type that must work from 11px app UI to campaign-scale display.

items.title: Stamps, labels, and codes: Vrints-Kolsteren rebrands a pizza restaurant on the move
items.summary: Antwerp studio Vrints-Kolsteren rebranded London pizzeria Napoli on the Road as 'NotR,' swapping Italian restaurant clichés for a transport-and-shipping visual language — monospaced type, stamps, labels — built entirely around the brand's story of constant motion and evolution.
items.why: A clean example of brief-led identity design: the system works because the designers started with a narrative (movement, transformation) rather than a category aesthetic — a useful model for how Cuemath's brand could anchor to its learning story rather than generic edtech conventions.
